supermarket.note: Buy shell-on, head-on prawns if you can find them.
Hokkien or lo mein style noodles are the match for this.

general.item: sambal oelek or other chili paste

tools.name: Small bowl
tools.note: Two small bowls are needed, one for soaking the vermicelli and one for the eggs.

tools.name: Pot
tools.note: A large pot is needed for making the prawn stock and poaching the seafood.

tools.name: Sieve
tools.note: Use a fine mesh sieve so the dry ingredients sift smoothly.

tools.name: Wok
tools.note: A 12-inch frying pan can be used in place of the wok.

steps.title: Prep all ingredients
points: Prepare everything before you turn on the stove.
Peel the prawns, keeping all the heads and shells, and devein them.
Slice the squid into 1/2-inch rings.
Mince the garlic.
Cut the chives into 2-inch lengths.
Rinse the bean sprouts.
Soak the vermicelli in warm water for 10 minutes, then drain.
Loosen the yellow noodles with your fingers.
Beat the eggs in a small bowl.
Cut the limes into wedges.

steps.title: Make the prawn stock
points: Make the stock in the large pot.
Heat 1 tablespoon of the oil over medium to high heat, add the prawn heads and shells, and fry for 4 to 5 minutes, pressing them with the spatula, until they turn red and smell toasted.
Add the water and the pork belly.
Bring to a boil, then lower the heat and simmer gently for 35 to 40 minutes, skimming off any scum, until the pork is tender when pierced with a knife.

steps.title: Strain and season the stock
points: Lift out the pork and set it aside to cool.
Strain the stock through the sieve into the heatproof bowl, pressing hard on the heads to get out all the liquid.
Rinse the pot, pour the stock back in, and stir in the fish sauce and white pepper.
You should have about 4 cups.
Keep it at a gentle simmer over low heat.
Slice the cooled pork thinly.

steps.title: Cook the prawns and squid
points: Add the peeled prawns to the simmering stock and cook for 1 to 2 minutes, until pink.
Lift them out with the slotted spoon.
Add the squid and cook for 1 minute, until it turns opaque, then lift it out.
Leave the stock on low heat.

steps.title: Fry the noodles
points: Fry the noodles in two batches, so the wok stays hot.
Heat 2 tablespoons of the oil in the wok over high heat until it shimmers.
Pour in half the eggs and stir for about 30 seconds, until just set.
Add half the garlic and stir for 20 seconds.
Add half the yellow noodles and half the vermicelli and toss for 1 minute.
Ladle in 1 cup of the stock and keep tossing for 3 to 4 minutes, until the noodles have absorbed most of it.

steps.title: Cook the first batch
points: Add half the bean sprouts, prawns, squid, and pork, with another 1/2 cup of stock.
Toss for 2 minutes, until everything is hot and the noodles are glossy and slightly wet.
Add half the chives and toss for 30 seconds more.
Divide between two plates.
Wipe the wok and repeat with the remaining ingredients.

steps.title: Serve with sambal and lime
points: Serve with a tablespoon of sambal and a lime wedge on each plate.
Squeeze the lime over the noodles and mix in the sambal as you eat.

troubleshooting.solution: The stock was weak. Fry the shells until they are fully red before adding water, and press every drop out of the heads when straining.

troubleshooting.problem: The noodles stew instead of frying
troubleshooting.solution: The wok was overloaded or not hot enough. Cook in two batches and wait for the oil to shimmer before adding the eggs.

troubleshooting.problem: The noodles turn dry and stick
troubleshooting.solution: They have soaked up all the stock. Add another ladle of hot stock and toss until they are moist again.

troubleshooting.problem: The prawns and squid are rubbery
troubleshooting.solution: Poach them only until pink or opaque, since they heat through again in the wok.
